title: Legislative districts of Agusan del Sur

{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}}
{{Politics of the Philippines}}
The '''legislative districts of Agusan del Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Agusan del Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Agusan del Sur's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Agusan del Sur's 2nd congressional district|second congressional districts]].

== History ==
{{further|Legislative districts of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative districts of Agusan}}
Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Agusan del Sur were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and [[Agusan (province)|Agusan]] (1935–1969).

Republic Act No. 4979, approved in a plebiscite held simultaneously with the [[1967 Philippine Senate election|1967 elections]], split the old Agusan Province into [[Agusan del Norte]] and [[Agusan del Sur]] and provided them each with a congressional representative.<ref name="RA4979">{{Cite web |last=Congress of the Philippines |date=June 16, 1967 |title=Republic Act No. 4979 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Agusan del Norte and Agusan del Sur |url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1967/ra_4979_1967.html |access-date=February 4, 2017 |website=The LawPhil Project}}</ref> In accordance with Section 7 of R.A. 4979, Agusan del Sur first elected its separate representative starting in the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1969 elections]].<ref name=RA4979/>

Agusan del Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned one representative, elected at large, to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]].

Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a lone congressional district,<ref>{{Cite web |last=1986 Constitutional Commission |date=February 2, 1987 |title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/ |access-date=November 19, 2017 |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}}</ref> and it elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]].

The approval of Republic Act No. 9508 on October 20, 2008, divided the province into two congressional districts,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Congress of the Philippines |date=October 20, 2008 |title=Republic Act No. 9508 - An Act Providing for the Reapportionment of the Lone Legislative District of the Province of Agusan del Sur |url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2008/ra_9508_2008.html |access-date=February 4, 2017 |website=The LawPhil Project}}</ref> which elected their separate representatives starting in the [[2010 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2010 elections]].

== Senatorial representation ==
{{further|Philippines's 12th senatorial district}}
Between 1916 and 1935, the territory of what is now Agusan del Sur (then part of the undivided province of [[Agusan (province)|Agusan]]) was represented in the [[Senate of the Philippines]] through the [[Philippines's 12th senatorial district|12th senatorial district of the Philippine Islands]]. However, in 1935, all senatorial districts were abolished when a unicameral [[National Assembly of the Philippines|National Assembly]] was installed under a new constitution following the passage of the [[Tydings–McDuffie Act]], which established the [[Commonwealth of the Philippines]]. Since the [[1941 Philippine Senate election|1941 elections]], when the Senate was restored after a [[1940 Philippine constitutional plebiscites|constitutional plebiscite]], all twenty-four members of the upper house have been elected countrywide [[at-large]].

== Congressional representation ==
{{main|Agusan del Sur's 1st congressional district|Agusan del Sur's 2nd congressional district}}
Agusan del Sur has been represented in the lower house of [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various Philippine national legislatures]] since 1987 through its [[Agusan del Sur's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Agusan del Sur's 2nd congressional district|second congressional districts]].

== Provincial board districts ==
{{main|Agusan del Sur Provincial Board}}
The municipalities of Agusan del Sur are represented in the [[Agusan del Sur Provincial Board]], the [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] (provincial legislature) of the province, through Agusan del Sur's first and second provincial board districts.
